title: WHEN THE ADVISORS SEE IT FIRST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the Lord their God. Do you not yet realise that Egypt is ruined?"" - Exodus 10:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people around Pharaoh can see what he cannot. Do you not yet realise that Egypt is ruined?

It has come to this. His own officials — the men whose jobs depend on pleasing him — are telling him the truth. That takes courage, and it also tells us how obvious the situation had become to everyone except the man in charge.

Pride blinds. That is its most dangerous feature. It is possible to be the only person in the room who cannot see what is happening.

This is why God gives us people. Proverbs says plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed (Prov 15:22). We were never meant to assess our own lives alone.

Ask yourself honestly: when did I last let someone tell me something I did not want to hear? Do the people around me feel free to disagree with me? A person who is never contradicted is not necessarily right — they may simply be feared.

Listen to the officials in your life. Sometimes God speaks through them before He speaks through anything else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who has been telling me something I have not wanted to hear?
2. Do the people close to me feel safe to disagree with me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me humility to listen to the people You have placed around me. Open my eyes to what others can already see. Amen.
